body:
incidents-bot: Pager: P1 — GPU pool 'eu-west-2-gpu-prod' queue length spiked above 9k and sustained >85% utilization for 12m. Autoscaler attempted 6 scale-outs; 4 failed with node registration errors. Impact: 10% of hosted requests 5xx. Paging oncall
Oncall Ryan: I'm on it — looking at autoscaler logs now. Marking incident active.
Maria K.: seeing a lot of `Xid` and `CUDA error` in driver logs from the new kernel/driver bundle that rolled last night. Noticed a large correlation with driver version 515.76 -> 525.x.
Jun Park: Confirm — `dmesg` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 78` and `oom-killer` events occasionally. attaching snippet:
Jun Park: ```
[ 1023.412345] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU is lost
[ 1023.412350] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 78, PID=12903, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1023.412355] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12903 (serve-worker) total-vm:1024000kB
```
Priya S.: Autoscaler logs show `register node timeout` when kubelet tries to join. Many nodes bounce during kubelet/gpu-plugin startup.
SRE-Auto: Autoscaler triggered `scaleUp` 6 times; cloud provider accepted 6 VMs but 4 never reached Ready state within 10m, marked `FailedJoin`.
Oncall Ryan: Rolling back recent driver on a single canary node to see if registration stabilizes. Can we cordon a subset to force traffic away?
EngRuntime: Recommend cordon + drain the 4 flapping nodes and roll them with driver 515.76 (known stable) for now. We have a hotpatch binary ready for the driver-rollback tooling.
Customer Ops: flagging customers in EU who reported 500s: CUST-1123, CUST-2019. CC account teams.
Oncall Ryan: Running command to cordon nodes with high Xid counts:
Oncall Ryan: `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide | grep eu-west-2 | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon`
Maria K.: also adding `--evict=grace=30s` to drain to avoid stuck pods holding kernels.
Jun Park: logs from one of the failed nodes (node-gpu-17):
Jun Park: ```
Time="2026-02-11T01:23:45Z" level=error msg="nvidia-device-plugin crashed: exit status 2"
stderr: "nvidia-smi: command not found\nNVRM: The 'nvidia' kernel module is not loaded"
```
Priya S.: Looks like driver load race condition during node boot. Cloud images updated last night included new kernel header packaging. When kubelet hits device-plugin before driver modules finish, plugin crashes and node fails join.
SRE-Auto: Temporarily lowering max surge attempts and extending `nodeReadyTimeout` to 18m to give driver longer to load. Pushing config now.
Oncall Ryan: Doing a controlled scale-out to eu-west-1 as fallback region for a subset of traffic. Updating routing policy to route 30% of requests to eu-west-1 model replicas.
EngRuntime: Be careful — models in fallback are smaller-capacity; expect higher latency for those routed requests. Also enable `auto-fallback` in routing policy to avoid 5xx for new requests.
Customer Ops: Noting that SLA alerts triggered for two customers. Opened ticket INC-4389 and sent initial blurb to affected customers.
Maria K.: Starting driver rollback job on two flapping nodes: `sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-515 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` then `kubectl uncordon`.
Oncall Ryan: After rollback on node-gpu-17: node rejoined, kubelet registered, `nvidia-smi` returns devices. Good sign.
Jun Park: However node-gpu-21 still shows `Xid 13` and kernel oops. Planning to isolate it and gather `kubectl logs --previous` + `journalctl -k`.
SRE-Auto: Autoscaler config patch applied — `nodeJoinTimeout=18m`, `consecutiveFailedJoinsBeforeBackoff=3`. New scale-outs will be throttled.
Oncall Ryan: Quick mitigation summary so far: 1) cordon & drain flapping nodes, 2) rollback driver to 515 on canaries, 3) route 30% to eu-west-1, 4) autoscaler backoff to avoid amplifying failure, 5) customer notification sent.
EngRuntime: We should also suspend low-priority batch work and preemptible runs to free up capacity for hosted traffic. Can ops pause those queues?
Priya S.: Pausing batch queues now: `apictl queue pause --name=batch-eu-west-2` — will relieve ~18% capacity usage.
Customer Ops: Notifying product teams and listing impacted customers with rough ETA for full remediation ~2-4 hours depending on rollback progress.
Maria K.: Found correlation: nodes created after 02:00UTC showing driver 525.x, older nodes still stable. Suggest cluster image rollback for autoscaler images until we push a fixed driver packaging.
EngRuntime: We're building a driver packaging fix to avoid kernel module race. ETA 3h. In the meantime, manual rollback + extended join timeout recommended.
Oncall Ryan: Status update to #incidents in 10m with current mitigations and customer impact. Leaving a sticky note in the escalation channel.
SRE-Auto: Monitoring: queue length decreased from 9.2k -> 4.0k after traffic shift + drains + batch pause. 5xx rate down from 10% -> 3.1%.
Jun Park: Captured crashdump from node-gpu-21: saving core to /var/crash/gpu-21-2026-02-11.tar.gz and uploading to objstore at s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3380001234/gpu-21.tar.gz
EngRuntime: Plan to roll all new nodes with driver 515 until packaging fix released. We'll open a PR to autoscaler config to pin image tag to `gpu-image:20260210-stable`.
Oncall Ryan: Declaring P1 for the incident; escalate to EngRuntime lead for coordination. Handoff to Priya S. for night coverage in 45m. If any sharp regressions (5xx >8%) re-pager immediate.
Priya S.: Taking over. Documenting runbook steps I've executed in the incident ticket.
Customer Ops: Sent follow-up emails to affected customers: summary + mitigations + link to support ticket INC-4389.
Maria K.: After rolling back ~10 nodes and pausing batch, latency median is back to baseline, p95 improving. We'll continue gradual rollbacks.
SRE-Auto: Autoscaler now obeying backoff; no new failed joins in last 20m.
Jun Park: We'll keep collecting driver traces and submit to vendor if reproducible.
Oncall Ryan: Thanks team. Leaving open until EngRuntime confirms packaging fix. Priya, ping me on handoff when you take full responsibility. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: Roger. I have the runbook, the rollback scripts, and the customer list. Monitoring alerts set.
incidents-bot: Incident P1 'gpu-pool-driver-rollout' recorded. Postmortem owner: EngRuntime. Please update incident timeline within 24h.
Customer Ops: Customers CUST-1123 and CUST-2019 acknowledged receipt; both set to priority support.
Oncall Ryan: Handoff complete at 3380005400. Leaving channel.
